function: Selects each BS's broadcast beam combination (codebook antenna weights) with MAPPO to maximize coverage; a C-GAN digital twin pre-validates the SINR and KPIs (p. 2, 6).
system: Multi-cell 3D massive MIMO OFDM downlink: 3 BSs with 8x8 UPA, 256 single-antenna UEs; 3509.76 MHz carrier, 240 subcarriers of 30 kHz; no RIS (p. 3, 7-8).
method: MAPPO multi-agent reinforcement learning (distributed actors, centralized critics, one agent per beam) in a C-GAN (WGAN-GP) digital twin fitted to 1024 sampled beam schemes (p. 5-6, 8).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa simulator, 3GPP Urban Macro channel and 3D antenna models (TR 38.901); 256 UEs in three hotspots; 1024 of 9261 beam schemes sampled as real data (p. 7-8).
test_conditions: One QuaDRiGa scenario for training and testing; sweeps of SINR threshold, period length, and generated samples, each trained to convergence; modes Env-Env, DT-DT, DT-Env (p. 8, 10-11).
baselines: Non-learned: random best, greedy, integer programming, differential evolution; learned: MADDPG, TD3 for beam selection, and a DNN KPI predictor for the digital twin (p. 9-11).
metrics: Coverage (share of UEs above SINR threshold), MMD of generated versus real SINR distributions, relative error of mean SINR, absolute error of coverage, training episodes (p. 8-11).
complexity: Worst-case time complexity of all algorithms in Table IV, DRL O(KMB) with B candidate beams; 1000 episodes of 100 timesteps; no FLOPs or runtime (p. 10).
openness: none; no code or data release mentioned, data generated with QuaDRiGa (p. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 7: "We adopt the QuaDRiGa simulator [32] to simulate a practical massive MIMO system according to the 3GPP Urban"; p. 8: "Macro channel model and 3GPP 3D antenna model [26]" ([26] is TR 38.901, p. 12).
q2_support: p. 10: "solution in the digital twin and validation in the practical environment (DT-Env)" is the same QuaDRiGa scenario of p. 8: "we collect real data that includes 1024 randomly chosen beamforming schemes". Unseen schemes are held-out data of one scenario; no new scenario, band, or site is tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "The proposed DRL based algorithm is superior to random best algorithm, greedy algorithm and differential evolution algorithm"; p. 11: "the proposed MAPPO based algorithm achieves the best coverage optimization performance" over MADDPG and TD3 (Fig. 9).
q4_support: p. 10: "The worst-case time complexity of all the algorithms is displayed in Table IV." The DRL entry is O(KMB); no FLOPs, parameter count, or measured runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 7: "We adopt the QuaDRiGa simulator [32] to simulate a practical massive MIMO system". The data are generated by the simulator; no link, DOI, public dataset, or code release is stated.
notes: Borderline function: coverage-oriented antenna weight optimization framed as network optimization, but the learned decision is broadcast beam selection from a codebook scored by SINR, so area 3 and not above_phy. The C-GAN synthesizes SINR distributions as a surrogate environment, not the channel. q2 is 0 because DT-Env checks the surrogate on the same scenario and each use case is run to convergence (p. 11).
